notes: ex:paymentDuty is named once and plays both of its RL2 roles (due2-workflows.md §3.1 root): rl2:prerequisiteDuty becomes odrl:duty on the permission, the precondition, and RL2's independent rl2:clause becomes odrl:obligation on the policy, a root obligation. As an obligation it is in force whenever ex:viewPrivilege matches the request (§5.2) and its status is reported; as a precondition it gates the permission. One atom, one member-scope instance (the default, profiles §2 point 9), so one payment fulfils both roles and serves every later view by Alice. The duty names ex:Alice, so only evidence with actor ex:Alice is a witness (§5.3); another customer's payment does not count (scenario 4). With no deadline the duty is never violated, so violations = deny would change nothing here. Scenarios 3 and 4 are added. Divergence: with no qualifying payment, RL2's prerequisite is Active, so the privilege contributes no permit and the decision is NotApplicable; due2 reports the route as Pending with ex:paymentDuty outstanding.

expected.why: ex:viewPrivilege is T. ex:ev1 is a witness for ex:paymentDuty: before effective_at, action ex:pay, object ex:PhotoLicence, actor ex:Alice, no signer restriction; the duty has no constraints, so it is T and the candidate is ready. ex:viewPrivilege matches, so the same duty is in force as a root obligation, with the same witness: fulfilled.
ex:Bob ⊑ ex:Alice is F, so ex:viewPrivilege is F and is no candidate; its duty is not evaluated (§5.5). No rule of the policy matches, so the obligation is not in force either.
ex:viewPrivilege is T; ex:paymentDuty has no witness, so it is F (outstanding) and has no deadline. The one alternative is pending. As a root obligation the duty is in force and outstanding.

ex:ev2's actor ex:Bob is not the duty's assignee ex:Alice, so it is no witness; with no witness the duty is outstanding and the permission's only route is pending; the in-force obligation is outstanding for the same reason.
